question: What does the box do to a range of ordinary strings: plain lowercase words, capitalized words, multi-word sentences, digits, mixed alphanumerics, punctuation, and empty/space input?
expect: No model exists yet, so this is a broad first look. If outputs equal inputs, it's identity. If case changes, it's case transformation (upper/lower/title). If words are reversed, reordered, or joined, it's word manipulation. If digits or punctuation are stripped/altered, it's filtering. If empty and space inputs return empty or unchanged, that suggests simple passthrough; if they error or return special strings, that reveals edge handling. Comparing 'hello' vs 'Hello' isolates case behavior, 'hello world' vs 'Hello World' isolates per-word capitalization, and 'abc123' vs '123' isolates digit handling.

question: Does the box treat punctuation and symbols as separate words (split on non-letters) or keep them attached, and how are multiple spaces / leading-trailing spaces handled?
expect: If split() is on whitespace only (current model), 'hello,world'->'lmKAdlrow,olleh', 'a  b'->'a lmKAb' (double space collapsed to one), '  hello  '->'lmKAolleh'. If it splits on non-alphanumerics, 'hello,world'->'olleh lmKAdlrow' and 'a-b c'->'a b lmKAc'. Comparing 'a  b' vs 'a b' and '  hello  ' vs 'hello' reveals whitespace normalization; punctuation cases distinguish the tokenizer.

question: Does the box split words on punctuation boundaries or only on whitespace, and where exactly does the 'lmKA' prefix attach when a token contains punctuation?
expect: If split is on whitespace only (current model), outputs keep punctuation attached: 'lmKAdlrow,olleh', ',olleh lmKAdlrow', 'lmKArab-oof', 'lmKArab.oof', 'lmKAereht!ih', 'lmKAc,b,a', 'z,yx lmKAc', 'ihg lmKAfed,cba', 'lmKA.dne', 'lmKA,trats'. If the box instead splits on non-letter characters, punctuation would appear as separate tokens and 'lmKA' would attach to the last letter-run (e.g. 'hello,world' -> 'olleh,lmKAdlrow' or similar). Comparing the two hypotheses on these ordinary punctuation cases will reveal the true tokenization rule.

question: Does the box treat tabs/newlines and other whitespace as word separators like spaces, and does it collapse them the same way?
expect: If tabs/newlines are treated like spaces (split() with no args), outputs will be 'a lmKAb', 'a lmKAb', 'a lmKAb', 'olleh lmKAdlrow', 'a b lmKAc', 'eno lmKAowt', 'x y lmKAz', etc. If only literal spaces split, tokens stay joined and get reversed/prefix differently (e.g. 'b\ta' with lmKA prefix). This distinguishes whitespace-class splitting from space-only splitting, which ordinary multi-space inputs cannot fully separate.

question: Does the box split on punctuation-only tokens or keep them attached, and how does the lmKA prefix attach when a token is entirely punctuation or when punctuation appears at the start of a token?
expect: Current model reverses each whitespace token and prefixes lmKA to the last token. If outputs match that (e.g. '...' -> 'lmKA...', 'a ...' -> 'a lmKA...', '!?' -> 'lmKA?!'), punctuation-only tokens are just ordinary tokens. If instead punctuation is stripped/ignored or handled specially, we'd see different outputs, revealing whether the box treats punctuation-only tokens as words.

question: Does the box split words on whitespace only (keeping punctuation attached) and simply reverse each whitespace-delimited token, or does it treat punctuation as part of the token in some other way — testing mixed punctuation placement within otherwise ordinary multi-word inputs?
expect: If the model is right, each whitespace token is reversed as a unit and lmKA prefixes the last token: e.g. 'hello, world!' -> ',olleh lmKA!dlrow', 'foo bar, baz' -> 'oof lmKA,rab zаb'... Specifically expected: [',olleh lmKA!dlrow', 'oof lmKA,rab zаb'? no] — corrected: 'foo bar, baz' -> 'oof ,rab lmKAzab'; 'a.b c!d' -> 'b.a lmKAd!c'; 'one two, three.' -> 'eno lmKA,owt lmKA.eerht'? No — only last token gets prefix: 'eno ,owt lmKA.eerht'. Any deviation, e.g. punctuation being moved to token boundaries or prefix attaching differently, would reveal a punctuation-splitting rule the model misses.

question: Does the box's tokenization/prefix behavior hold for typical sentence-like inputs with mixed capitalization, digits, and punctuation at word boundaries, and does it treat multiple consecutive spaces in the middle consistently?
expect: If the model is right: 'ehT kciuq nworb lmKAxof', ',olleH lmKA!dlrow ?uoy era woH', 'I evah 3 lmKA.selppa', '...tiaW lmKA?tahw', 'sey on lmKAebyam', 'liamE em ta lmKA.moc@b@a', ':ecirP lmKA99.5$', 'eno owt lmKAeerht', '1A 2B lmKAC3', 'dooG ,gninrom lmKA!enoyreve'. Any deviation (e.g., digit handling, $/@ treatment, multiple-space collapsing, or capitalization affecting reversal) reveals a wrong assumption about ordinary sentence inputs.

question: Does the box strip trailing whitespace (so trailing spaces/tabs/newlines do not create an empty final token), and does it handle leading whitespace the same way while preserving internal multiple spaces as single separators?
expect: If trailing whitespace is stripped like leading whitespace (as E2's '  hello  ' -> 'olleh lmKA' suggests, since no trailing empty token appears), outputs should be 'lmKAolleh' for 'hello ', 'hello  ', 'hello\t', 'hello\n'; 'lmKAolleh' for ' hello' and '  hello'; 'a lmKAb' for 'a b '; 'a lmKAb' for ' a b'; 'a lmKAb' for 'a  b  '; and 'olleh lmKAdlrow' for ' hello world '. If instead trailing whitespace produces a trailing empty token prefixed with lmKA (as the current model predicts: 'lmKAolleh lmKA'), that reveals a leading/trailing asymmetry and corrects the model's lstrip-only behavior.

question: Does the box treat a run of internal whitespace as a single separator (collapsing) while preserving leading/trailing stripping, and does it handle mixed internal whitespace (tabs/newlines among spaces) as one separator producing a single space between reversed tokens?
expect: If runs of any whitespace collapse to one separator (as model v3 predicts), outputs will be like 'a b lmKAc', 'a b lmKAc', 'a b lmKAc', 'a b lmKAb', 'a b lmKAb', 'eno owt eerht lmKAruof', 'x lmKAy', 'p q r lmKAs', 'dna d aer lmKAliart' (leading stripped, trailing stripped), 'a b lmKA'. Any deviation — e.g. empty tokens from tabs/newlines or preserved double spaces — would reveal that only literal spaces are collapsed or that some whitespace types are not separators, refining the tokenizer model.

question: How does the box handle strings consisting only of whitespace (spaces, tabs, newlines, mixed), which is the one ordinary input class the model has never actually observed—predicting 'lmKA' for empty input but never testing whitespace-only input?
expect: If whitespace-only input behaves like empty input after stripping, all outputs should be 'lmKA'. If it instead produces an empty token list joined to nothing, outputs would be ''. Any non-'lmKA' result (e.g. empty string, or a lone prefix) would reveal a special case in how stripping and empty-token handling interact, which the model currently assumes but has never verified on pure-whitespace inputs.
